label: early-middle step (t=3-5) first occurrence of o/3/r or <DEL>, after w/e/u/k/0-type prefix
explanation: Sparse update-gate unit that fires only at steps t=3..6 (peak t=4) and never in the copy phase after the delimiter. About 70% of its mass is in the original phase, on the first occurrence of a small set of input tokens (o, 3, r, plus weaker z, p). The other 30% is on the <DEL> step when L is 3..6. Within that window, how often and how strongly it fires depends on which tokens came earlier. The top activations follow prefixes containing w (prev_tok=w gives 8x lift), e, u, k or a leading digit 0/1. Example: 0 e a w [r]. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) almost never fire. The window-and-token condition alone covers about 94% of activation mass but has only about 3% precision. Adding a prefix-composition condition raises precision to about 10%, at the cost of mass recall, which drops to about 0.66. Firing looks like a graded threshold crossing over a weighted mix of prefix tokens that a simple boolean cannot capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=w (+3.40), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=z (+2.73), orig0=0 (+2.39), prev2_tok=w (+2.29), phase=0 & in_tok=o (+2.23), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=o (+2.23). Lower it: phase=2 (-6.56), prev3_tok=- (-5.05), t=8 (-4.13), t=9 (-3.92).
